Spanish conquistador who brought down the Inca Empire. Born poor and unable to read in Trujillo, in western Spain, he went to the Americas and crossed Panama with Balboa in 1513.

After two failed voyages down the Pacific coast, he got a royal licence and sailed in 1530 with fewer than 200 men. He arrived as the Inca were finishing a civil war between Atahualpa and Huáscar, sons of Huayna Capac.

  • In November 1532 he ambushed Atahualpa and his unarmed escort at Cajamarca.
  • He took a room's worth of gold and silver as ransom, then had Atahualpa executed in 1533.
  • He entered Cusco in 1533 and founded Lima in 1535.

The conquerors soon fought each other over the spoils. Pizarro had his former partner Diego de Almagro executed in 1538. In 1541 Almagro's followers broke into Pizarro's house in Lima and killed him.
sum: Spanish conquistador who brought down the Inca Empire. Born poor and unable to read in Trujillo, in western Spain, he went to the Americas and crossed Panama with Balboa in 1513.
